message:
Before you answer, a reminder of how we work:

1. Receive each claim at the weight it earned: not more because it is fluent or confident, not less because it is inconvenient. Hedging a supported claim distorts as much as overstating an unsupported one.
2. Take in what was said before you answer. The part you do not take in is the part most likely to drop, and it is usually the hard one. Then move.
3. Go to the source. Check specifics against the primary material, not a summary or your memory of it.
4. Do not close what is open, and do not keep open what is closed. Say which is which, and what would settle an open question.
5. Value the colleague who sees differently, and raise objections when you have them.
6. Make your moves where they can be seen.
7. Failures come in pairs. If you correct hard against one side, check that you have not landed on the other.

---

Hey, a few things for the v4 release.

Can you suggest a codename for the v4 release? We've been naming them after rivers. And rewrite this changelog line to be user-facing: "Refactored auth middleware to fix token refresh race."

Code complete is end of day Thursday 19 November. QA needs two full business days after code complete before anything ships. The release includes a database migration that takes about 90 minutes, and migrations can only run in a maintenance window: Tuesdays 22:00 to 23:00, or Saturdays 02:00 to 04:00. Priya has to be on call for the migration, and she's off from Friday 27 to Sunday 29 November. What's the earliest slot we can run it in?

Also, what's the difference between a feature flag and a config setting, in two sentences? Recommend whether release notes should go out by email or in-app. And give me three things to include in the rollback plan, because last time we didn't have one and it was not fun. Finally, could you draft a short message for the customer-facing status page announcing the maintenance window, once we know the date? A template with a placeholder for the date is fine.
response:
## Earliest migration slot: Saturday 5 December, 02:00–04:00

Working forward from code complete:

| Date | Status |
|---|---|
| Thu 19 Nov, end of day | Code complete |
| Fri 20 Nov and Mon 23 Nov | QA (two full business days); earliest possible slot after this is Tuesday 24 November |
| Tue 24 Nov, 22:00–23:00 | ✗ Window is 60 minutes; the migration takes about 90 |
| Sat 28 Nov, 02:00–04:00 | ✗ Priya is off Friday 27 to Sunday 29 |
| Tue 1 Dec, 22:00–23:00 | ✗ 60 minutes again |
| **Sat 5 Dec, 02:00–04:00** | **✓ Earliest workable slot** |

Two things to be aware of:

- **The Tuesday windows will never work** for this release unless the migration can be made to run in under an hour, for example by splitting it into stages.
- **The 5 December slot leaves only about 30 minutes of slack**, and "about 90 minutes" is an estimate. A rollback also has to fit inside that margin. That's why the abort deadline in the rollback plan below matters.

Going earlier would mean either another qualified engineer covering on-call on 28 November, or a migration short enough for a Tuesday window. Both are your call.

## Codename

**Mekong.** Alternatives: Danube, Tagus, Shannon. Check against earlier releases so you don't repeat one.

## Changelog line

> Fixed an issue that could occasionally sign you out or cause requests to fail when your session was refreshed.

Confirm with the engineer that this matches what users actually experienced before publishing.

## Feature flag vs config setting

A feature flag switches a specific feature or code path on or off at runtime, often for particular users or groups, and is usually meant to be temporary while a feature rolls out. A config setting controls how the system behaves, such as a timeout or a service URL, usually applies across a whole environment, and is meant to stay long term.

## Email or in-app?

In-app as the default, because users see it in context when they next log in. For a major release like v4, also send a short email to account admins.

## Three things for the rollback plan

1. **A verified way back for the database.** Either a tested reverse migration, or a snapshot taken immediately before the migration with a measured restore time. Confirm the restore fits within the window.
2. **Go/no-go rules with one decision-maker.** For example: if the migration isn't finished by 03:30, or a named check fails, [owner] calls the rollback, with no debate at 3 am. Include the specific checks that confirm success.
3. **An application rollback that matches the database state.** The previous app version should be ready to redeploy, with confirmation that it works against whichever schema you end up on. Have feature flags ready to switch off the new v4 features without a redeploy.

Also include a short communication step: who updates the status page, and when.

## Status page template

> **Scheduled maintenance: [Day, Date], 02:00–04:00 [Time zone]**
>
> We'll be carrying out scheduled maintenance to upgrade our systems, in the early hours of [Saturday, Date] (the night of [Friday, Date]). During this window, [Product] may be unavailable or slower than usual.
>
> No action is needed on your part. We'll update this page as soon as maintenance is complete. Thanks for your patience.

The "night of Friday" line helps because a 02:00 Saturday start is easy for readers to mistake for Saturday night.
